prompt: How can I calculate the circumference of the moon?
response:
To calculate the circumference of the Moon, you can use the formula for the circumference of a circle, which is \(C = 2\pi r\), where \(C\) is the circumference and \(r\) is the radius of the circle. For the Moon, you need to know its radius.

The average radius of the Moon is approximately 1,737 kilometers. Using this value, you can calculate the circumference as follows:

\[C = 2 \times \pi \times 1,737 \text{ km}\]

Using \(\pi \approx 3.14159\),

\[C \approx 2 \times 3.14159 \times 1,737 \text{ km}\]
\[C \approx 10,921 \text{ km}\]

So, the approximate circumference of the Moon is about 10,921 kilometers.
